faqs.q: What is the difference between PCM and PCB in the Science stream?
faqs.a: PCM means Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, the combination needed for engineering entrance exams such as JEE and for courses like architecture. PCB means Physics, Chemistry and Biology, needed for medical entrance through NEET and for many life-science courses. Some students take all four subjects to keep both options open, though the workload is heavier.

faqs.q: Can I study Maths in the Commerce or Humanities stream?
faqs.a: Yes, in many schools. Most boards let Commerce and Humanities students take Mathematics as an elective, and CBSE also offers Applied Mathematics, which is geared towards commerce, economics and statistics. Which subjects you can combine depends on what your school offers, so check before you finalise your stream.

faqs.q: Can I change my stream after Class 11 or Class 12?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is easier in some directions than others. Changing in Class 11 is usually only possible early in the year with your school's permission. After Class 12, Science students can move into most Commerce or Humanities degrees, but entering courses like engineering or medicine needs the right Science subjects in Class 12.

faqs.q: Which stream is best for government jobs?
faqs.a: Any stream can lead to a government job. Major exams such as the UPSC civil services, SSC graduate-level exams and bank officer exams ask for a graduate degree in any discipline, so the stream you choose after Class 10 does not shut you out. Only some technical and specialist posts need a particular subject or degree.
